page: Google Cloud Platform c4a-highmem-64 is an Arm64-based server instance powered by the Neoverse-V2 processor. It features 64 dedicated physical cores with a single thread per core, providing 64 vCPUs. The instance is equipped with 512 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or integrated GPUs, and has zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

In benchmark testing, the c4a-highmem-64 demonstrates strong multi-core capabilities and exceptional memory performance. Its multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and passmark memory scores rank in the top tier, supported by a cached read-only memory bandwidth of 7912.04 GB/sec. Database operations and Redis SET performance are also top-tier, with Redis achieving 134.03 million operations per second. Single-core performance, such as stress-ng single-core CPU testing, remains in the average tier.

This instance is highly suited for memory-intensive workloads, high-throughput database operations, and static web serving. It also performs well in lightweight LLM inference tasks, particularly for prompt processing. However, the lack of local storage requires external block storage attachment, and the absence of AVX or AMX instruction sets limits its suitability for specialized x86 vector math or hardware-accelerated machine learning workloads. The Arm64 architecture offers a resource-dense, cost-efficient profile for scaled enterprise deployments.
